article.title: Proceratium silaceum
article.extract: Proceratium silaceum is a species of ant in the family Formicidae.

turns.guesser:
This looks like a tiny ant from the USA that preys on spider eggs, orange-yellow in colour, with an upside-down feature (a curled-under gaster?) and living in leaf litter. That matches the genus Proceratium. "Orange-yellow" suggests croceum (saffron), though it could be silaceum or pergandei. Is the article about the genus, or one species?

GUESS: Proceratium croceum

You mean one species, not named after a person (so not pergandei), and the colour is ochre, an earth pigment. That points to silaceum.

GUESS: Proceratium silaceum
